summary.answer: Source-visible answer: the batch postinit driver, the terminal point of the ordering graph. It iterates the whole registry: for each entry run the requirement resolver (88) and spawn exec_post_system (89); after iterating set the level flag system_init_complete (92) - the signal every system::wait_till blocks on - and destroy the registry (93), without a join proving postfunc completion. register can recreate the cleared table; clearing does not prove lifetime inactivity. Its single caller is the native level_finalizeinit event handler codecallback_finalizeinitialization (callbacks_shared.gsc 1095 / csc 502). Sequence inside one native event: run_post_systems() THEN callback(#on_finalize_initialization) (1096) - so wz_open_skyscrapers gsc/csc on_finalize_initialization handlers (registered at wz_open_skyscrapers.gsc 47 / .csc 27; bodies gsc 129-133 / csc 81-85 leading to the wzheavymetalheroes-gated hmh_ramp dynent enable function_7276b578 gsc 160-175) are dispatched after the driver has spawned its batch, set the flag and cleared the registry; this does not establish that all spawned postfuncs have completed. Exact native-entry boundary: the event name and handler annotation event_handler[level_finalizeinit] (callbacks_shared.gsc 1093) are source-recorded; the engine call site and event order are not - recorded as the exact minimum evidence request.
summary.behavior: Batch postinit driver. run_post_systems(): foreach over level.system_funcs calling function_5095b2c6(func) (requirement resolver) and spawning thread exec_post_system(func) per entry (86-90); then level flagsys::set("system_init_complete") (92) and level.system_funcs = undefined (93). The set() both flags completion and notifies all waiters (flagsys_shared.csc 9-18: self.flag[str]=1; self notify(str)); the registry is cleared only after the foreach returns - the spawned exec_post_system threads run against records that were just deleted from the array but remain valid via the func references captured in the spawn calls. Sole caller: callbacks_shared event_handler[level_finalizeinit] codecallback_finalizeinitialization (gsc 1093-1097 / csc 500-504), which calls run_post_systems() first and THEN dispatches callback(#"on_finalize_initialization") to all add_callback registrants (dispatch mechanism callbacks_shared.gsc 17-25, 60-107). The registry is undefined after the driver; register() can recreate it, so lifetime inactivity is not established. util_shared.gsc::__main__ waits on this flag while its postfunc is still incomplete.

summary.answer: Source-visible answer: postinit invocation body; skips undefined, ignored or already-postdone entries; an eligible !postdone branch resolves requirements before setting the marker, with no recheck after that resolver and no proved prereq-stage scheduling or exactly-once guarantee, sets postdone BEFORE invoking postfunc (49-50), and the bounded literal caller query finds run_post_systems (89) and the post-requirement resolver function_5095b2c6 (69/76) in the supplied twins; this does not prove absence of indirect, dynamically selected or native callers. Dependency 'wait' is fire-and-forget thread spawn, not a join. Ordering graph: level_finalizeinit -> run_post_systems -> foreach [function_5095b2c6 asserts predone||ignore, thread exec_post_system(func)] -> postfunc bodies run as spawned threads; run_post_systems requests the flag, without joining postfunc completion, by setting flag system_init_complete (92) AFTER all threads are spawned, then the registry is cleared (93). HMH linkage: wz/HMH postfuncs (e.g. util_shared __main__ via system::wait_till, load consumers) synchronize on that flag; wz_open_skyscrapers on_finalize_initialization (hmh_ramp dynent enable) is dispatched only after this phase by codecallback_finalizeinitialization callbacks_shared.gsc 1096. summary.behavior: Postinit invocation executor. exec_post_system(func): returns when the record is undefined or func.ignore is set (37-40) - ignore-flagged systems never get postinit; if !func.postdone: if func.reqs is defined it calls function_5095b2c6(func) first (44-47), then sets func.postdone=1 BEFORE synchronously invoking [[func.postfunc]]() (49-50). The marker precedes the postfunc call, so a later entry with the same unchanged truthy marker skips that branch. The resolver precedes the marker and has no following guard recheck; actual scheduling, reentry during prerequisite work, crashes and marker mutation remain unverified. The bounded literal caller inventory shows thread launches rather than synchronous calls: run_post_systems spawns it per entry (system_shared.csc 89) and function_5095b2c6 spawns it per requirement (69, 76). The supplied twins contain the same literal caller locations (35-52, 69, 76, 89). The postfunc bodies are therefore executed inside spawned threads whose completion is not awaited individually; the unjoined dispatch phase requests the global flag through run_post_systems' flagsys::set("system_init_complete") at line 92 after the foreach and only then level.system_funcs=undefined (93).
